task: Add the drop-branch, dev-only accept-schema, project-view and list/read/edit file MCP tools to the Assistant MCP server (plan --like 9)

analysis.objective: Add four more tools to the `adops mcp` Assistant server (drop-branch, dev-only accept-schema, a read-only project view, and list/read/edit file tools), each behind the same dev/Branch allow-list guard, sanitized error mapping and secret-leak tests, and require plain Pipeline names in every tool that takes one; the second slice of vision item 7.
analysis.successDefinition: Done when ALL hold: (1) the server lists exactly run, preview, validate, drop_branch, accept_schema, project_view, list_files, read_file and edit_file. (2) drop_branch removes only br_<branch>__ schemas through drop_project_branch, fails at once with a sanitized 'busy' reply when stage's Warehouse lock is held (ASSISTANT_LOCK_TIMEOUT), and the CLI keeps its 30-minute wait (asserted). (3) accept_schema acts only on the Environment named exactly dev (stage, prod, qa, Dev, 'dev ', custom names, and any branch are refused before anything is touched), takes no Warehouse lock, and is refused when dev shares a database with stage or prod. (4) Every tool taking a pipeline argument (run, preview, validate, accept_schema) refuses names that are empty or contain '/', '\\' or '..' before any file is read. (5) project_view returns Pipelines with Steps, Environments, Schedules and, per Secret Reference, only 'set' or 'missing', never a value or host/user/database. (6) read_file and list_files stay inside pipelines/, dbt/ and adops.yaml after resolve (no '..', no symlink escape), refuse .env and .env.* in any case, and replace every resolved Secret Reference value with *** in file text; edit_file writes only under pipelines/ and dbt/ and never adops.yaml or .env. (7) Every new tool's responses, on success and on each failure path, pass assert_no_secret. (8) CI stays green: uv sync --locked, ruff, 100% line+branch coverage, no new pragma, no mcp/typer imports in domain/application, no new template files and no new E2E case.
assumptions: User decision: drop_branch fails fast on a held stage Warehouse lock with the same ASSISTANT_LOCK_TIMEOUT as run/preview; drop_project_branch gains a lock_timeout parameter defaulting to the CLI's DEFAULT_LOCK_TIMEOUT (30 minutes), so the CLI is unchanged.
User decision: accept_schema is dev only and takes no Warehouse lock, because it only writes dev's recorded schema shape.

User decision: project_view is read-only and shows, per Secret Reference, only its status (set or missing), through a new secret_reference_status helper in application/secrets.py; it never shows a value.

User decision: read_file refuses .env and .env.* outright (any letter case, checked again after resolve) and in every other file replaces any value of a resolved Secret Reference with ***; list/read resolve the path and re-check it is inside the Project, with no symlink escape and no '..'.
User decision: edit_file may write only under pipelines/ and dbt/; adops.yaml and everything else is read-only for the Assistant.

Confirmed: every MCP tool taking a pipeline argument requires a plain Pipeline name (no '/', '\\', '..'); this closes the open blocker that run's pipeline argument reads pipelines/<name>.yaml unchecked. Planned in the accept-schema phase because that phase adds the next pipeline-taking tool.

Planner assumption (to keep the binding 2026-11-21 decision intact): read and list use the allow-list pipelines/, dbt/ and adops.yaml, so .adops/, .github/ and server/ stay refused; the user's .env and redaction rules apply on top. If the user wants read to cover the whole Project folder, only the read roots in allowed_project_path change.
Repo fact: dbt runs with a temporary --profiles-dir (dbt_transform.py:139), so editing dbt/profiles.yml cannot redirect a connection; no extra guard for that.

The pure path rule allowed_project_path lives in domain/assistant_access.py and works on strings only (the domain purity test bans pathlib); the filesystem resolve-and-recheck lives in a new interface module assistant_files.py.

Branch Environments are allowed for drop_branch because a Branch Environment lives in stage's Warehouse by design (ADR-0006); the tool still refuses every Environment argument other than a branch name and never drops a non-br_<branch>__ schema.

Tool replies stay TypedDicts, tools stay synchronous, and exceptions are mapped by the existing _sanitized_errors; WarehouseUnreachable and StepError are added to it where a new tool can raise them (they are not in RUN_ERRORS).
New MCP behaviour is tested with the in-memory client/server session and assert_no_secret from tests/unit/interface/mcp_harness.py; no stdio or E2E test is added.
adops.yaml, pipeline and dbt text are never trusted to be secret-free, so file text is redacted using the values resolved from the Project's .env merged with the process environment at call time.
risks: Path checks are easy to get subtly wrong: symlinked parents, a symlink inside pipelines/ pointing at .env, case-insensitive macOS names (.ENV, Pipelines/), and '..' after resolve. The pure rule must be applied to the requested path and again to the resolved path.

Redaction by value replacement can miss a value embedded in a larger secret, or break on an empty or very short value; an empty value must never be replaced, and longer values must be replaced before shorter ones.

drop_project_branch is the only existing use case that takes a Warehouse lock without a timeout path; changing its signature can break existing stubs (the horizon-9 run phase broke test_run_command and conftest the same way).
accept_schema connects to dev's Source and Warehouse, so a dev that shares a database with stage could overwrite stage's recorded shape unless the shared-connection guard runs first.
Secret leaks can come through new channels: project_view (connection details), read_file (literal passwords in allowed files), edit_file echoing content back, and error text built from exceptions.
Tool calls run one at a time, but edit_file writes files while run reads them; whole-file writes are not atomic, so a crash can leave a half-written Pipeline file.
outOfScope: Run logs and the read-logs tool: they need a new log writer and a new adapter, so they get their own horizon.
The test-connection tool: it needs new ports and adapters that open every Source, Warehouse and target.
accept-schema --branch: branch baselines start fresh (known gap, horizon 6).
ADR-0015 accepted-change records and Git-based Breaking Change acceptance: the record format is undecided.
Hardening Promotion, clearing runs left STARTED after a Server crash: Server concerns, deferred with the Promotion blockers.
Any non-stdio MCP transport or MCP authentication: v1 is local stdio only.
Claude Code's real MCP tool-call timeout against long runs: needs real use first.
Editing adops.yaml, .env, .adops/, .github/ or server/ through the Assistant: deliberately read-only or refused.
Git operations from the MCP server: the skills do Git (ADR-0009, ADR-0011).
analysis.domainShapeReason: The work enforces DataOps rules a domain expert recognizes: the Assistant acts only in dev and Branch Environments, a Secret Reference never reveals its value, and only some Project files are editable; MCP is only the transport.

ubiquitousLanguage.meaning: The user's own AI coding tool (for example Claude Code) that operates the product through the MCP server.
One operation the server exposes to the Assistant (run, preview, validate, drop_branch, accept_schema, project_view, list_files, read_file, edit_file).
A disposable Environment for one Git branch, built from stage's settings in br_<branch>__ Branch Schemas in stage's Warehouse.
A sanitized error returned by server code, before anything is touched, when a request names a disallowed Environment, Pipeline name or path.
The name of a secret used in configuration in place of its value; the Assistant may see the name and whether it is set, never the value.
The per-Warehouse lock a run takes; the Assistant's tools try it once and reply 'busy' instead of waiting.
A Source shape change a run stops on until the user accepts the new shape; accept-schema records the accepted shape for dev.

discoveryFindings.finding: build_server(project) registers synchronous tools; guarded_run_arguments re-reads adops.yaml per call and applies assistant_target then refuse_shared_dev_connection; _sanitized_errors maps WarehouseLocked, AssistantRefusal and RUN_ERRORS to fixed text and anything else to 'unexpected <Type>'; ASSISTANT_LOCK_TIMEOUT = 0.
discoveryFindings.implication: Each new tool is a few lines on top of these helpers; WarehouseUnreachable and StepError are not in RUN_ERRORS and must be added to the mapping.

discoveryFindings.finding: mcp_harness provides write_project (writes a .env with a distinctive value for every Secret Reference incl. alert_webhook_env), call_tool, error_text and assert_no_secret(result, secrets).
discoveryFindings.implication: All new tool tests use these; the horizon-9 ledger shows a grade lost points for a call_tool without assert_no_secret.

discoveryFindings.finding: drop_project_branch(project, branch) takes build_warehouse_lock(warehouse, project, STAGE) with the default timeout (30 minutes); the CLI maps PipelineValidationError, ProjectFileError, MissingSecretError, WarehouseLocked and WarehouseUnreachable to fixed text.
discoveryFindings.implication: Add a lock_timeout keyword defaulting to DEFAULT_LOCK_TIMEOUT; the MCP tool passes ASSISTANT_LOCK_TIMEOUT; WarehouseUnreachable needs its own mapping in _sanitized_errors.

discoveryFindings.finding: accept_project_schema(project, pipeline, table, environment) reads adops.yaml and pipelines/<pipeline>.yaml, builds the Sync and snapshot store, takes no Warehouse lock, and returns AcceptedSchema; the CLI maps StepError and WarehouseUnreachable.
discoveryFindings.implication: The tool passes 'dev' only, after guarded_run_arguments; StepError joins _sanitized_errors; no lock is added (user decision).

discoveryFindings.finding: run_command.read_project_files and validate_command._pipeline_files build pipelines/<name>.yaml from the raw name with no check.
discoveryFindings.implication: plain_pipeline_name must run before the guard in run, preview, validate and accept_schema.

discoveryFindings.finding: resolve_secret_references treats an empty value as missing; secret_references(warehouse, sources, targets) lists password references; alert_webhook_env is a separate reference; project_env merges .env under the process environment.
discoveryFindings.implication: secret_reference_status and the redaction values follow the same rule and the same merged environment.

discoveryFindings.finding: test_domain_purity bans os, sys, io, pathlib, random, time, subprocess, socket and sqlite3 in src/adops/domain; test_application_purity guards application/.
discoveryFindings.implication: allowed_project_path and plain_pipeline_name are string-only; resolve and file I/O live in interface/assistant_files.py.

discoveryFindings.finding: In horizon 9 adding lock_timeout to run_project broke stubs in tests/unit/interface/conftest.py and test_run_command.py (unplannedFiles); FakeLocks.build already records timeouts.
discoveryFindings.implication: Plan updates to stubs of drop_project_branch / build_warehouse_lock in the drop-branch phase instead of finding them at the gate.

phases.name: Add the drop-branch MCP tool
phases.goal: The Assistant can drop a Branch Environment through a drop_branch MCP tool that calls drop_project_branch, fails at once with a sanitized busy reply when stage's Warehouse lock is held, and never touches stage's own schemas. The CLI keeps its 30-minute lock wait.
phases.rationale: This is one small slice across layers (rule, use case, adapter, MCP entry point and tests) built on the pattern horizon 9 already settled, instead of spreading it over several phases. It also gives drop_project_branch the lock_timeout path that run_project already has, so the Assistant never hangs on a held lock while the CLI behaviour stays the same.
filesAffected: tests/unit/interface/conftest.py (only if the FakeLocks or stub signatures need the new keyword)
changes: Add `lock_timeout: float = DEFAULT_LOCK_TIMEOUT` to drop_project_branch in drop_branch_command.py and pass it to run_command.build_warehouse_lock(warehouse, project, STAGE, lock_timeout). The `drop_branch` CLI command passes nothing, so it keeps the 30-minute wait.

Add a synchronous `drop_branch(branch: str)` tool in build_server. It calls assistant_target(None, branch) first, then drop_project_branch(project, branch, lock_timeout=ASSISTANT_LOCK_TIMEOUT), inside `_sanitized_errors()`. It never calls the CLI function and never takes an Environment argument.
Add a DroppedBranchReply TypedDict (environment, dropped schema names) and a small serializer from DroppedBranch.

Extend _sanitized_errors with WarehouseUnreachable ('stage's Warehouse is unreachable or locked by another process' style fixed text, naming no host or DSN), because it is not in RUN_ERRORS and would otherwise reply 'unexpected WarehouseUnreachable'.

Tests in test_mcp_server.py: a branch drop returns the dropped schema names; an empty branch name is refused; a held lock gives the busy reply with FakeLocks.timeouts == [ASSISTANT_LOCK_TIMEOUT]; a missing stage Warehouse Secret Reference names only the variable; an unreachable Warehouse gives the fixed text; an unexpected error names only its type; stage's own schemas are untouched (fake WarehouseSchemas records only br_ names). Every call_tool is followed by assert_no_secret.

Tests in test_drop_branch_command.py: the CLI drop_branch passes DEFAULT_LOCK_TIMEOUT to the lock (FakeLocks.timeouts == [DEFAULT_LOCK_TIMEOUT]); update any stub of drop_project_branch or build_warehouse_lock that rejects the new keyword (the horizon-9 run phase broke conftest.py and test_run_command.py the same way).
phases.expectedResult: A drop_branch MCP tool that fails fast on a held stage lock, with the CLI default unchanged, covered by in-memory tests with secret-leak assertions.
guardNotes: g3: every new branch (busy, unreachable, missing secret, unexpected) has a unit test; no pragma.
g6: mcp imported only in interface/; no application change.
g2: ruff line length 100 on the new reply TypedDict and messages.
phases.compensation: Remove the drop_branch tool and the lock_timeout parameter; the CLI path is unchanged by default.

rubric.label: The MCP drop fails fast while the CLI still waits 30 minutes
rubric.ruleStatement: The drop_branch tool passes ASSISTANT_LOCK_TIMEOUT to drop_project_branch and gets an immediate busy reply on a held stage lock; the CLI command passes no timeout and so uses DEFAULT_LOCK_TIMEOUT. 10 = both timeouts are asserted through FakeLocks.timeouts and the busy reply text is asserted. 8 = the MCP busy reply is asserted but the CLI default is not. Below 8 = the default was changed for the CLI or the MCP tool can wait.
passCriteria: A test holds the lock via FakeLocks(error=WarehouseLocked('stage', 0)) and asserts the exact busy reply text and FakeLocks.timeouts == [ASSISTANT_LOCK_TIMEOUT].
A test of the CLI drop_branch command asserts FakeLocks.timeouts == [DEFAULT_LOCK_TIMEOUT].
`grep -n 'lock_timeout' src/adops/interface/drop_branch_command.py` shows a keyword with the default DEFAULT_LOCK_TIMEOUT, not a literal 0 or 1800.
failureExamples: The new keyword defaults to 0, so the CLI drop no longer waits for a running stage run and fails in CI.
The tool is tested only with a lock that is free, so the busy path is never exercised.

rubric.label: The tool can only drop br_<branch>__ schemas and refuses a bad branch name
rubric.ruleStatement: The tool accepts only a branch name (no Environment argument), refuses an empty name through assistant_target, and relies on the existing exact-prefix drop so stage's own schemas are never dropped. 10 = tests show the fake WarehouseSchemas received drop calls only for br_ names while stage's schemas are listed, and an empty name is refused before any lock or Warehouse call. 8 = prefix behaviour is shown but the empty-name refusal is not asserted before side effects. Below 8 = the tool takes an Environment or builds the prefix itself.
passCriteria: A test lists stage schemas plus br_<branch>__ schemas in the fake and asserts only the br_ ones were dropped.
A test with branch '' asserts the refusal text and zero lock, schema and state calls.
The tool signature in the in-memory tool list has only a `branch` property.
failureExamples: The tool builds `f'br_{branch}__'` itself and a branch named like a stage schema prefix drops the wrong schemas.
An empty branch reaches drop_project_branch and the refusal comes from deep inside as 'unexpected ...'.

rubric.label: Every response and error is sanitized and scanned for secrets
rubric.ruleStatement: Every call of the drop_branch tool, on success and on each failure path (missing stage Warehouse Secret Reference, unreachable Warehouse, held lock, unexpected error, empty branch), passes assert_no_secret with distinctive values for every Secret Reference, and each exception the use case can raise maps to a fixed sanitized message, never 'unexpected <Type>' for a known error and never raw exception text. 10 = every call_tool in the new tests is followed by assert_no_secret and each mapped exception has its own test. 8 = all success and refusal paths scanned but one mapped exception is untested. Below 8 = a failure path returns raw exception text or is never scanned.
passCriteria: `grep -c 'call_tool(' tests/unit/interface/test_mcp_server.py` is not larger than `grep -c 'assert_no_secret(' tests/unit/interface/test_mcp_server.py` for the new tests (every call is scanned).
Each exception type the tool can raise has a test asserting the exact reply text, not just isError.
A test whose use-case stub raises an unexpected exception shows the reply names only the type.
failureExamples: A refusal test calls call_tool and checks isError but skips assert_no_secret, the exact gap the horizon-9 run-tool grade found (7/9).
A known error such as WarehouseUnreachable falls into the generic branch and replies 'unexpected WarehouseUnreachable' because _sanitized_errors was not extended.

rubric.label: Rules live in domain/application, the entry point only wires
rubric.ruleStatement: The drop_branch tool in mcp_server.py only calls the guard, one existing or new use-case function and a reply serializer; every rule it applies sits in domain/assistant_access.py, application/ or a named interface helper, and no domain or application module does I/O or imports mcp/typer/os.environ.  10 = purity tests pass, the tool body is a few lines, and every rule has its own unit test. 8 = rules are in the right layer but one lives in a long tool body. Below 8 = a path, name or Environment rule is written inline in the tool, or domain code touches the filesystem.
passCriteria: `uv run pytest tests/unit/domain/test_domain_purity.py tests/unit/application/test_application_purity.py` passes.
`grep -n 'import mcp\|from mcp' -r src/adops` lists only src/adops/interface/mcp_server.py.
The drop_branch tool body contains no string comparison of an Environment name, path or Pipeline name; those calls sit in named helpers with their own unit tests.
failureExamples: The tool checks `'/' in pipeline` or `name.startswith('.env')` inline, so the rule has no domain-level test and the next tool copies it differently.
A domain helper calls Path.resolve() or reads a file, which the purity test only catches if pathlib is imported.

phases.healerHint: The likeliest failure is a stub or FakeLocks signature that rejects the new lock_timeout keyword; accept it in the stub and assert the CLI default, as horizon 9 did.

In mcp_server.py call plain_pipeline_name first in run, preview, validate (when pipeline is given) and the new tool, before the guard reads adops.yaml and before any file is read.

Add a synchronous `accept_schema(pipeline, table, environment=None, branch=None)` tool. It takes no Warehouse lock and never passes a timeout.

Add an AcceptedSchemaReply TypedDict (pipeline, table, step, environment, column count, nullable column names) and a serializer from AcceptedSchema; no column types or values beyond names already in the Warehouse shape.
Extend _sanitized_errors with StepError (its message is already free of secrets) so a failing Source or Step has a fixed reply; keep unexpected errors as the type name only.
Domain tests: one test per refused name ('', '..', 'a/b', 'a\\b', '../x', 'x..y', a NUL name) and accepted names ('shop_sync', 'a-b', 'v2'), and the refusal text does not contain the supplied name.

MCP tests: accept_schema in dev succeeds and records the shape; stage, prod, qa, production, Dev, 'dev ', a custom name and any branch each get a refusal with zero build_* calls; a dev sharing a database with stage is refused; FakeLocks records no lock call (documenting the no-lock decision); Source unreachable, a missing Secret Reference and a StepError map to fixed text; run, preview, validate and accept_schema each refuse '../adops' and 'a/b' with no file read. Every call_tool is followed by assert_no_secret.
phases.expectedResult: An accept_schema MCP tool for dev only, a plain_pipeline_name rule applied to every pipeline-taking tool, and tests with refusals and secret-leak assertions.
guardNotes: g3: every refusal branch of plain_pipeline_name and the branch-given refusal is tested; no pragma.
g6: domain/assistant_access.py stays free of pathlib, os and mcp (test_domain_purity bans them).
g2: ruff passes on the new TypedDict and messages.
phases.compensation: Remove the accept_schema tool and the plain_pipeline_name calls; the existing tools return to their earlier behaviour.

phases.name: Add the read-only project-view MCP tool
phases.goal: The Assistant can read a Project overview through a project_view MCP tool: Pipelines with their Steps, Environments, Schedules when present, and for each Secret Reference only whether it is set or missing, never a value.
phases.rationale: This is one small slice across layers (rule, use case, adapter, MCP entry point and tests) built on the pattern horizon 9 already settled, instead of spreading it over several phases. changes: Add `allowed_project_path(relative: str) -> str` to domain/assistant_access.py. phases.name: Add the edit-file MCP tool

phases.rationale: This is one small slice across layers (rule, use case, adapter, MCP entry point and tests) built on the pattern horizon 9 already settled, instead of spreading it over several phases. changes: Extend allowed_project_path with a keyword `write: bool = False`. Add `write_project_file(project, relative, content) -> bool` to interface/assistant_files.py. It applies allowed_project_path(write=True) to the request, resolves the deepest existing ancestor and requires it inside project.resolve() and allowed_project_path(write=True) again on the resolved target, refuses a target that is an existing directory or a symlink leaving the allowed folders, creates missing parent folders inside the allowed root, writes the UTF-8 text, and returns whether the file was created.

Add a synchronous `edit_file(path: str, content: str)` tool and an EditFileReply TypedDict (path, bytes written, created). The reply never echoes the content. A content larger than a fixed size cap gets a fixed refusal before any write. The tool does not run validate; the Assistant calls validate itself.
